title: Mor Barsawmo
source_text:
Mar Barṣawmo riše dabile, yatúmowa. 
U+babo māṯ, i+emo šqila ḥreno ŭ mbela ʕam ruḥa. 
Ḥəfla ŭ mašəġla, hawi tlaṯ+šnaye.
Azzé, qrele ŭ kṯule, qrele ŭ kṯule. 
Saləq yawmo li+goro, behn diḏe ʕayəq. 
Šaməʕ̥ qole dar+ruʕye. 
(Kəmmina, d̥koṯən kəmṭən aḥ+ḥayewən mu+ṭuro. 
Ar+ruʕye, kəmmina, komarʕәn aʕ+ʕeze bu+ṭuro. 
Kuḏʕat, kofǝhmat?) 
Aṯən, azzé, omar, ‘Kazzí gabayye dməštaʕeno tre+xabre aʕmayye, behn diḏi rowaḥ’.
Ak+kalbe dar+ruʕye ḥzalle, heš... lar+ruʕye lə+ḥzalle, ak+kalbe ḥzalle, azzéhəlle. 
Azzéhəlle, mədde ŭ xəḷḷe ŭ nkətte ŭ mgavlačče.
Xaləṣ karwan bu+qawlawo bi+qriṯayo. 
Əmmi, ‘ʕAǧaba hano arnuwe ṣǝdle, hano ṭaʕle ṣǝdle u+qa…ak+kalbani hawxa kosaymi
K̬madiqi ʕul mu+syoġo, bi+arʕo kḥayri ga kalé zʕuro bayn al+lappat dak+kalbe, kalé zʕuro bayn al+lappat dak+kalbe. 
Azzehən. 
Aḥ+ḥaṭroṯaṯṯe, žxwa ḥaṭro d̥qayse kowe aʕmayye d̥koqulʕi a+ḥmore. 
Kətwa ḥaṭroṯe aʕmayye, mlalle qəm ṣadrayye kefe
Ŭ azzə́n, maḥatte ʕal ak+kalbanək, maḥtǝnne. 
Maḥatte, maḥatte, maḥatte aʕlayye, šqəlle u+zʕuro mənne. 
Šqəlle u+zʕuro mənne. 
Koḥayri, mətwile, lo admo, lo naparušk̇e, lo aǧ+ǧulayḏe qṭiʕi, lo mede, xud ruḥe.
Əmmi, ‘Komət̬haymnina b Aloho’. 
Ḥa mənne, ‘Hano ṭowo d Alóhoyo, dak+kalbani hawxa səmme ebe ŭ lo+ǧarile mede’. 
U+ḥreno komar, ‘Komət̬haymanno, b Aloho, d̥kətyo hano qadišo rabo. 
Dak+kalbe hawxa səmme u+ʕaǧobano ebe, lo aǧ+ǧulayḏe qṭiʕe, ŭ lo ǧarutk̇e, lə+nkətte, lo admo xār mine. 
Hano ṭowo d Alóhoyo’. 
Ŭ azzehən, azzehən, aṯi híyeste lu+bayto, aṯi lu+bayto, lo bmede. 
Malaxle, omar, ‘Gəzzí li+barriye, ʕobadno šan Aloho’. 
Malaxle, azzé li+barriye. 
Laqi lnahro dmaye, nahro kobe pelat, maye semoqe. 
Kozayəʕ̥, mdayšalle lu+baxyo, yatu, mdayšalle lu+baxyo. 
Lo+maǧrele moḥe bayn am+mayanək, naʕímowa. 
Mdayšalle lu+baxyo. 
L Aloho mtarasle malaxo, məḷḷe, ‘Zux, šāl be i+niyayḏe mənyo’. 
U+malaxo naḥət xud i+stune mi+šmayo, mḥele ruḥe bŭwā́r di+ṭalane. 
Səmle ruḥe nošo, ŭ azzé gabe bu+šəklayḏe. 
Komar, ‘Šlomo aʕlux, abro! 
Mə‿kosaymat harke, brazi, abro?’ 
Komar, ‘B̥šayno, bәšlomo, ʕammo, b̥xēr aṯət, may‿koṯat?’ 
Omar, ‘Ma mə‿kosaymat harke?’
Mdayšalle lu+baxyo, omar, ‘Ono zʕuro, yatúmono, babi māṯ, emi šqila ḥreno ŭ mbélali ʕam ruḥa. 
Uʕdo kobaʕno əzzino, ṣoyamno, mṣaleno šan Aloho’. 
Omar, ‘Yaʕni gdobat ṣōz, ddoʕat ŭ mṣalat šan Aloho?’ 
Omar, ‘Ṣōzyo. 
Hul d̥kətli ʕəmro, ono mṣaleno ŭ mṣaleno, ṣoyamno šan Aloho’. 
Omar, ‘D‿itúx bəṯri’. 
Azzé bəṯre, mbele. 
Omar, ‘Naʕímohat, dǝzzúx li+barriye, gməšḥoṭat. 
Izúx, gəmbannux ldayro’.
Azzé, mbele ldayro, kal kīt dayroye ŭ məlfone ŭ riš dayroyo, ʕam i+ʕaṣriye, ʕam u+noqušo dʕaṣriye. 
Drele šlomo, ‘B̥šayno, bәšlomo, ʕammo. 
Xēryo?’
Omar, ‘Ašə́r, u+zʕurano, yatúmoyo. 
Ŭ māṯ u+babo, ŭ li+emo šqila ḥreno, kubʕo, kubʕo… Kobaʕ̥ d̥koṯaw ŭ qore, yolaf dәmṣale šan Aloho’. 
Ḥǝrre ga zʕuro xušk̇o, hawxa lavhati ŭ saxi. 
Omar, ‘ʕAla ʕayne, ʕammo, ʕala ʕayne!’ 
Lǝḏʕiwa d̥kətyo malaxo. 
Omar, omar, ‘Kazzí bxa <ṭәr dәṯxu>..., fayšutu bәšlomo!’ 
Əmmi, ‘ʕAmmo, ʕaṣríyeyo, gəzzúx layko? 
Fuš ádlalyo gaban’. 
Omar, ‘Ašə́r, gəzzino. 
Lo+ḥaruli’ ... Saləq. 
Nafəq i+darga ŭ hawi xud̥ stune, saləq li+šmayo u+malaxo.
Fāš u+zʕuro gabayye. 
(Ánnaqqa meqəm ṣopat mani latwa). 
Sōmwa i+nuraṯṯe, konašwa u+qaṭmaṯṯe, ŭ mṭéwalle maye, sōmwa k̇elik̇at ʕal iḏayye, qorewa ŭ koṯáwwaste. 
Qrele, kṯule, hawi šamošo. 
Mi+šamošuṯo hawi dayroyo. 
Mu+dayroyo hawi riš dayroyo. 
Hawi riš dayroyo. 
Arbʕi+dayroye nafəl taḥt iḏe. 
Ánnaqqa u+ʕamo xd‿i+masale duʕdo nafəlwa baḥ+ḥṭohe, nafəlwa baḥ+ḥtohe. 
Əzzewa kul+lalyo lәqriṯo, korazwa aʕlayye, mofaqwa... madʕárwalle mšiḥoye. 
Yawmo mḥele b̥qarʕe d̥ṭuro. 
Kətwa qriṯo b̥qarʕe d̥ṭuro, mḥele bi+kaše. 
Naqqa aṣ+ṣalme, aʕ+ʕasekər daṣ+ṣalme šridi, əmmi, ‘Kaṯi Barṣawmo, kmazər aṣ+ṣalmayḏan’. 
Ŭ šridi ʕam gabe ŭ mčanqalle ad+dargat dlo+ʕəbri ... dlo+ʕobar li+walaye. 
Omar, ‘Darban raḥúqoyo, kobaʕno mənxu d̥fətḥutu ad+dargat. 
Aḥna šafóʕena ŭ silaḥe latlan ŭ lə+k̬maze…’ Əmmi, ‘Dlo+mazirat aḥna ŭ aṣ+ṣalmayḏan’. 
Omar, ‘Ašə́r, lə+gmazərno lo hatu ŭ lo aṣ+ṣalmaṯxu, ono zlām ʕabódono, kobaʕno d̥fətḥutu ad+dargat, šafóʕena, gəzzano’. 
Hedik̇a ftəḥḥe ad+dargat, azzé hul fəlga di+walaye, komalxi ʕam gabe. 
Omar, ‘Uʕdo məǧġalno xabro du+šayno. 
Mə‿kəmmutu?’ 
Əmmi, ‘Dməǧġolat dlo+mazirat aṣ+ṣalmayḏan, məǧġál!’ 
Omar, ‘ʕÁǧaba, uʕdo ʕal mə‿kowutu idara b̥qarʕe du+ṭurano našifo? 
ʕAl mə‿kowutu idara?’
Əmmi, ‘Ašə́r, ġắlăbe hawina šapərzá. 
Hani arbaʕ+əšnaye maṭro laṯilan, ŭ an+nahrat raḥúqene. 
Kuzzano baṫ+ṫanak̇e, bas+sablat, ba+ḥmore, kəmṭina maye. 
Ġắlăbe hawina šapərzá’.
Omar, ‘Uʕdo ṭolabno mu+alohayḏi doṯe maṭro aʕlayxu. 
Lo+kәmt̬haymnutu ebe?’ 
Əmmi, ‘Bele’. 
Ġắlăbe aṯile ʕәšq. 
Hiye ŭ ann+arbʕi dayroyayḏe čiki b̥ḥarbo, mṣalalle ŭ brəkke ŭ ṭləbbe, ‘Ya u+morayḏan, dhat marḥmat ʕal i+walayaṯe, balki mhaymni’. 
 ‘Ma i+saʕaye ba məqqa?’  
Omar, ‘I+saʕaye bat+tarte ŭ falge’. 
Hedik̇a hawyo tarte du+lalyo, pežə́n lawi. 
Ánnaqqa ḥəngi d Mar Barṣawmo brəkle, mṣalele, baṭəl, marfele hawxa, gnele hawxa ʕal i+anišk̇ayḏe. 
Ḥəlle, ḥzele kәkwo bi+šmayo. 
Omar, ‘Xud̥ koḥozeno u+kәkwano bi+šmayo, Alóhoste koḥozeli mžido’.
(Arbaʕ ŭ ḥamši+šnaye səmle ʕəmro, lә+mžīd ŭ lo+daməx. 
Maḥatwa qariše dab+basmore ʕal ḥaṣe dlo+domax ŭ mḥalaqwa u+ḥawlo lkaṯpoṯe, fōšwa qimo dayəm qəm Mšiḥo.)
Omar, ‘Ăḷ... Mšiḥo…xud̥ ḥzeli u+kәkwawo, lә Mšíḥoste ḥzéleli mžido’. 
Qayəm, dʕele, ṭləble. 
Hawi saʕaye ḥḏo, ḥḏo ŭ falge, tarte. 
Əmmi, ‘Haaa, Barṣawmo mdaglono! 
Koyo u+maṭro dl Aloho mṭelelan? 
U+alohayḏux koyo?’ 
Naqqa qayimo i+hawa taḥtayto baq+qudrat d Aloho. 
Ŭ aṯən aʕ+ʕaywe xd‿aq+qatore, ŭ hawən aṭ+ṭavat ŭ mḥele lu+maṭro. 
Bat+tarte ŭ falge dmərre, mḥele lu+maṭro, arbʕo+yawme, ŭ arbʕo+lalye. 
Malən ag+gubone, malən ab+bašqoqone, malən hne. 
 Kəmmi, ‘Barṣawmo, marle lu+alohayḏux dәmbaṭal u+maṭrano’. 
Omar, ‘Ašə́r dlo+tawrutu aṣ+ṣalmaṯxu, suġḏútəlle, ṭoreno dmaḥrawxu’. 
Azzə́n twərre.
Maṭi u+xabro lu+qašo, lu+qašaṯṯe. 
Kə́twayle tarte+bnoṯe, ġắlăbe roḥámwalle, u+qašaṯṯe.
Nafiqi li qamaytayḏe, əmmi, ‘Barṣawmo, mǝ‿kubʕat? 
Manqaṣlux i+ʕaskar dbabayna’. 
Omar, ‘Klawu bdukṯayxu’.
Zriʕi bayn li+arʕo ŭ li+šmayo. 
Fayiši hawxa haykle. 
Lappe lo+məǧġoli, lo+qaymi, lo…haw… Fayiši hawxa haykle.
Maṭi u+xabro lu+qašo, u+qašo ġắlăbe roḥamwa a+bnoṯe. 
Aṯi, mžīd qəm raġle d Mar Barṣawmo. 
Maḥatle u+ʕafro draġle d Mar Barṣawmo ʕal qarʕe druḥe ŭ sġəḏle l Mar Barṣawmo, omar, ‘Kobaʕno d̥šorat a+bnoṯayḏi’. 
Omar, ‘Məšrewu!’ 
Naqqa šarən. 
Ŭ azzə́n, edi twərre aṣ+ṣalmaṯṯe ŭ mət̬haymanne, mət̬haymanne bә Mšiḥo ŭ hawən səryoye. 
Ŭ hun žә mə ra sāġ.

sentences.translation: He had become scared, he started crying, he sat down, he started crying.

items.value: Kozayəʕ̥, mdayšalle lu+baxyo, yatu, mdayšalle lu+baxyo.

sentences.source_line: Lo+maǧrele moḥe bayn am+mayanək, naʕímowa.
sentences.translation: He didn’t dare plunge into that water, he was a child.

items.value: He didn’t dare plunge into that water, he was a child.

sentences.source_line: Mdayšalle lu+baxyo.
sentences.translation: He started crying.

sentences.source_line: L Aloho mtarasle malaxo, məḷḷe, ‘Zux, šāl be i+niyayḏe mənyo’.
sentences.translation: God sent an angel to him, he said, ‘Go and ask him what his intention is’.

sentences.source_line: U+malaxo naḥət xud i+stune mi+šmayo, mḥele ruḥe bŭwā́r di+ṭalane.
sentences.translation: The angel went down like a pillar from the sky, and he threw himself in front of a thicket.

items.value: U+malaxo naḥət xud i+stune mi+šmayo, mḥele ruḥe bŭwā́r di+ṭalane.

sentences.source_line: Səmle ruḥe nošo, ŭ azzé gabe bu+šəklayḏe.
sentences.translation: He made himself a human, and he went to him in his likeness.

items.value: Səmle ruḥe nošo, ŭ azzé gabe bu+šəklayḏe.

sentences.translation: He says, ‘Peace upon you, my son!

items.value: He says, ‘Peace upon you, my son!

items.value: What are you doing here, nephew, son?’

sentences.translation: He says, ‘Hello, welcome, uncle, peace be upon you, where are you coming from?’

items.value: Komar, ‘B̥šayno, bәšlomo, ʕammo, b̥xēr aṯət, may‿koṯat?’

sentences.source_line: Omar, ‘Ma mə‿kosaymat harke?’
sentences.translation: He says, ‘What are you doing here?’

items.value: He says, ‘What are you doing here?’

sentences.source_line: Mdayšalle lu+baxyo, omar, ‘Ono zʕuro, yatúmono, babi māṯ, emi šqila ḥreno ŭ mbélali ʕam ruḥa.
sentences.translation: He started crying, he says, ‘I am a child, an orphan, my father has died, my mother took another one and took me with her.

items.value: Mdayšalle lu+baxyo, omar, ‘Ono zʕuro, yatúmono, babi māṯ, emi šqila ḥreno ŭ mbélali ʕam ruḥa.

sentences.source_line: Uʕdo kobaʕno əzzino, ṣoyamno, mṣaleno šan Aloho’.
sentences.translation: Now I want to go, to fast, to pray on God’s behalf’.

items.value: Uʕdo kobaʕno əzzino, ṣoyamno, mṣaleno šan Aloho’.
Now I want to go, to fast, to pray on God’s behalf’.

sentences.source_line: Omar, ‘Yaʕni gdobat ṣōz, ddoʕat ŭ mṣalat šan Aloho?’
sentences.translation: He says, ‘Like, do you give me your word that you will bless and pray on God’s behalf?’

items.value: Omar, ‘Yaʕni gdobat ṣōz, ddoʕat ŭ mṣalat šan Aloho?’
He says, ‘Like, do you give me your word that you will bless and pray on God’s behalf?’

sentences.source_line: Omar, ‘Ṣōzyo.
sentences.translation: He says, ‘It’s a promise.

sentences.source_line: Hul d̥kətli ʕəmro, ono mṣaleno ŭ mṣaleno, ṣoyamno šan Aloho’.
sentences.translation: As long as I have life, I shall keep praying and praying, fasting on God’s behalf’.

items.value: Hul d̥kətli ʕəmro, ono mṣaleno ŭ mṣaleno, ṣoyamno šan Aloho’.
As long as I have life, I shall keep praying and praying, fasting on God’s behalf’.

sentences.source_line: Omar, ‘D‿itúx bəṯri’.
sentences.translation: He says, ‘Come on, come after me’.

items.value: He says, ‘Come on, come after me’.

sentences.source_line: Azzé bəṯre, mbele.
sentences.translation: He went after him, he took him.

items.value: He went after him, he took him.

sentences.source_line: Omar, ‘Naʕímohat, dǝzzúx li+barriye, gməšḥoṭat.
sentences.translation: He says, ‘You are a child, if you go to the wilderness, you’ll get dehydrated.

items.value: He says, ‘You are a child, if you go to the wilderness, you’ll get dehydrated.

sentences.source_line: Izúx, gəmbannux ldayro’.
sentences.translation: Go, I’ll take you to a monastery’.

items.value: Go, I’ll take you to a monastery’.

sentences.translation: He went, he brought him to a monastery, here there are monks and teachers and an abbot, in the evening, with the evening bell (i.e., at 6 pm).

items.value: Azzé, mbele ldayro, kal kīt dayroye ŭ məlfone ŭ riš dayroyo, ʕam i+ʕaṣriye, ʕam u+noqušo dʕaṣriye.
He went, he brought him to a monastery, here there are monks and teachers and an abbot, in the evening, with the evening bell (i.e., at 6 pm).

sentences.source_line: Drele šlomo, ‘B̥šayno, bәšlomo, ʕammo.
sentences.translation: He extended greetings. ‘You’re welcome, (come) in peace, uncle.

items.value: He extended greetings. ‘You’re welcome, (come) in peace, uncle.

sentences.source_line: Xēryo?’
sentences.translation: How are you (lit. ‘is it good’)?’

sentences.source_line: Omar, ‘Ašə́r, u+zʕurano, yatúmoyo.
sentences.translation: He says, ‘Really, this boy is an orphan.

items.value: He says, ‘Really, this boy is an orphan.

sentences.source_line: Ŭ māṯ u+babo, ŭ li+emo šqila ḥreno, kubʕo, kubʕo… Kobaʕ̥ d̥koṯaw ŭ qore, yolaf dәmṣale šan Aloho’.
sentences.translation: And his father died, and his mother married another man, she wants, she wants... He wants to read and write, to learn to pray for God’s sake’.

items.value: Ŭ māṯ u+babo, ŭ li+emo šqila ḥreno, kubʕo, kubʕo… Kobaʕ̥ d̥koṯaw ŭ qore, yolaf dәmṣale šan Aloho’.
And his father died, and his mother married another man, she wants, she wants... He wants to read and write, to learn to pray for God’s sake’.

sentences.source_line: Ḥǝrre ga zʕuro xušk̇o, hawxa lavhati ŭ saxi.
sentences.translation: They looked, here’s a beautiful young man, so good-looking and complaisant.

items.value: Ḥǝrre ga zʕuro xušk̇o, hawxa lavhati ŭ saxi.
They looked, here’s a beautiful young man, so good-looking and complaisant.

sentences.source_line: Omar, ‘ʕAla ʕayne, ʕammo, ʕala ʕayne!’
sentences.translation: He says, ‘At your service (lit. ‘upon eyes’), uncle, at your service!’

items.value: He says, ‘At your service (lit. ‘upon eyes’), uncle, at your service!’

sentences.source_line: Lǝḏʕiwa d̥kətyo malaxo.
sentences.translation: They did not know that he was an angel.

items.value: They did not know that he was an angel.

sentences.translation: He says, he says, ‘I am going by <your leave>, goodbye!’

items.value: Omar, omar, ‘Kazzí bxa <ṭәr dәṯxu>..., fayšutu bәšlomo!’
He says, he says, ‘I am going by <your leave>, goodbye!’

sentences.translation: They say, ‘Uncle, it is evening, where are you going?

items.value: They say, ‘Uncle, it is evening, where are you going?

sentences.source_line: Fuš ádlalyo gaban’.
sentences.translation: Stay with us tonight’.

sentences.source_line: Omar, ‘Ašə́r, gəzzino.
sentences.translation: He says, ‘Really, I’ll go.

sentences.source_line: Lo+ḥaruli’ ... Saləq.
sentences.translation: It doesn’t bother me’. He went up.

items.value: It doesn’t bother me’. He went up.

sentences.source_line: Nafəq i+darga ŭ hawi xud̥ stune, saləq li+šmayo u+malaxo.
sentences.translation: He went through the gate and became like a pillar, the angel went up to heaven.

items.value: Nafəq i+darga ŭ hawi xud̥ stune, saləq li+šmayo u+malaxo.

sentences.source_line: Fāš u+zʕuro gabayye.
sentences.translation: The boy stayed with them.

sentences.source_line: (Ánnaqqa meqəm ṣopat mani latwa).
sentences.translation: Now then, back then there were none of these stoves (lit. ‘stoves from these’).

items.value: Now then, back then there were none of these stoves (lit. ‘stoves from these’).

sentences.translation: He would do their fires, sweep their ashes, and bring water to them, do chores at their command (lit. ‘their hands’), he would also read and write.

sentences.source_line: Qrele, kṯule, hawi šamošo.
sentences.translation: He read, he wrote, he became a deacon.

items.value: He read, he wrote, he became a deacon.

items.value: From deaconship, he became a monk.

sentences.translation: From the monk, he became an abbot.

items.value: From the monk, he became an abbot.

sentences.translation: He became an abbot.

sentences.translation: Forty monks fell under his control (lit. ‘hand’).

items.value: Forty monks fell under his control (lit. ‘hand’).

sentences.translation: Now then, people, just like today’s situation, they had fallen into sin (lit. ‘the sins’), they had fallen into sin.

items.value: One day, he struck off for a mountaintop.

items.value: Kətwa qriṯo b̥qarʕe d̥ṭuro, mḥele bi+kaše.

sentences.translation: He says, ‘Really, I won’t harm either you or your idols, I’m a man of worship, I want you to open the gates, we are passers-by, we shall go’.

items.value: He says, ‘Now, I’ll say something peaceful (lit. ‘a word of peace’).

items.value: They say, ‘If you speak, if you don’t harm our idols, speak!’

sentences.translation: He says, ‘I wonder, on what do you manage on this dry mountaintop?

items.value: They say, ‘Really, we became very miserable.

sentences.translation: He would put straps of nails on his back so he wouldn’t lie down, and he would toss a rope onto his shoulders, he would always stay upright before Christ.

items.value: Maḥatwa qariše dab+basmore ʕal ḥaṣe dlo+domax ŭ mḥalaqwa u+ḥawlo lkaṯpoṯe, fōšwa qimo dayəm qəm Mšiḥo.)
He would put straps of nails on his back so he wouldn’t lie down, and he would toss a rope onto his shoulders, he would always stay upright before Christ.

sentences.source_line: Omar, ‘Ăḷ... Mšiḥo…xud̥ ḥzeli u+kәkwawo, lә Mšíḥoste ḥzéleli mžido’.
sentences.translation: He says, ‘By Go... Christ… just as I saw that star, Christ also saw me stretched out’.

items.value: Omar, ‘Ăḷ... Mšiḥo…xud̥ ḥzeli u+kәkwawo, lә Mšíḥoste ḥzéleli mžido’.
He says, ‘By Go... Christ… just as I saw that star, Christ also saw me stretched out’.

sentences.source_line: Qayəm, dʕele, ṭləble.
sentences.translation: He stood up, he prayed, he petitioned.

items.value: He stood up, he prayed, he petitioned.

sentences.source_line: Hawi saʕaye ḥḏo, ḥḏo ŭ falge, tarte.
sentences.translation: It turned one o’clock, one and a half, two o’clock.

items.value: Hawi saʕaye ḥḏo, ḥḏo ŭ falge, tarte.
It turned one o’clock, one and a half, two o’clock.

sentences.source_line: Əmmi, ‘Haaa, Barṣawmo mdaglono!
sentences.translation: They say, ‘Aha! Barsawmo the deceiver!

sentences.source_line: Koyo u+maṭro dl Aloho mṭelelan?
sentences.translation: Where is the rain that God has brought us?

items.value: Where is the rain that God has brought us?

sentences.source_line: U+alohayḏux koyo?’
sentences.translation: Your God, where is he?’

sentences.source_line: Naqqa qayimo i+hawa taḥtayto baq+qudrat d Aloho.
sentences.translation: At once the east wind (lit. ‘lower wind’) rose through God’s powers.

items.value: Naqqa qayimo i+hawa taḥtayto baq+qudrat d Aloho.
At once the east wind (lit. ‘lower wind’) rose through God’s powers.

sentences.source_line: Ŭ aṯən aʕ+ʕaywe xd‿aq+qatore, ŭ hawən aṭ+ṭavat ŭ mḥele lu+maṭro.
sentences.translation: And clouds like boulders came, and there were thunderclaps and rain struck.

items.value: Ŭ aṯən aʕ+ʕaywe xd‿aq+qatore, ŭ hawən aṭ+ṭavat ŭ mḥele lu+maṭro.
And clouds like boulders came, and there were thunderclaps and rain struck.

sentences.source_line: Bat+tarte ŭ falge dmərre, mḥele lu+maṭro, arbʕo+yawme, ŭ arbʕo+lalye.
sentences.translation: At half past two, as they said, rain struck, four days and four nights.

items.value: Bat+tarte ŭ falge dmərre, mḥele lu+maṭro, arbʕo+yawme, ŭ arbʕo+lalye.
At half past two, as they said, rain struck, four days and four nights.

sentences.source_line: Malən ag+gubone, malən ab+bašqoqone, malən hne.
sentences.translation: The cisterns filled up, the alleys filled up, some whatsits filled up.

items.value: Malən ag+gubone, malən ab+bašqoqone, malən hne.
The cisterns filled up, the alleys filled up, some whatsits filled up.

sentences.source_line: Kəmmi, ‘Barṣawmo, marle lu+alohayḏux dәmbaṭal u+maṭrano’.
sentences.translation: They say, ‘Barsawmo, tell your God to stop this rain’.

items.value: They say, ‘Barsawmo, tell your God to stop this rain’.

sentences.source_line: Omar, ‘Ašə́r dlo+tawrutu aṣ+ṣalmaṯxu, suġḏútəlle, ṭoreno dmaḥrawxu’.
sentences.translation: He says, ‘Really, if you do not break your idols, worship him, I’ll let him destroy you’.

items.value: Omar, ‘Ašə́r dlo+tawrutu aṣ+ṣalmaṯxu, suġḏútəlle, ṭoreno dmaḥrawxu’.
He says, ‘Really, if you do not break your idols, worship him, I’ll let him destroy you’.

sentences.source_line: Azzə́n twərre.
sentences.translation: They went, they broke them.

sentences.source_line: Maṭi u+xabro lu+qašo, lu+qašaṯṯe.
sentences.translation: The news reached the priest, their priest…

items.value: The news reached the priest, their priest…

sentences.source_line: Kə́twayle tarte+bnoṯe, ġắlăbe roḥámwalle, u+qašaṯṯe.
sentences.translation: He had two daughters, he loved them very much, their priest.

items.value: He had two daughters, he loved them very much, their priest.

sentences.source_line: Nafiqi li qamaytayḏe, əmmi, ‘Barṣawmo, mǝ‿kubʕat?
sentences.translation: They went out to meet him, they say, ‘Barsawmo, what do you want?

items.value: They went out to meet him, they say, ‘Barsawmo, what do you want?

sentences.source_line: Manqaṣlux i+ʕaskar dbabayna’.
sentences.translation: You have reduced our father’s army!’

items.value: You have reduced our father’s army!’

sentences.source_line: Omar, ‘Klawu bdukṯayxu’.
sentences.translation: He says, ‘Stand still in place (lit. ‘on your place’)’.

items.value: He says, ‘Stand still in place (lit. ‘on your place’)’.

sentences.source_line: Zriʕi bayn li+arʕo ŭ li+šmayo.
sentences.translation: They froze between the earth and heaven.

items.value: They froze between the earth and heaven.

sentences.source_line: Fayiši hawxa haykle.
sentences.translation: They remained so, statues.

sentences.source_line: Lappe lo+məǧġoli, lo+qaymi, lo…haw… Fayiši hawxa haykle.
sentences.translation: They can neither talk, nor get up, nor … anymore. They remained so, statues.

items.value: Lappe lo+məǧġoli, lo+qaymi, lo…haw… Fayiši hawxa haykle.
They can neither talk, nor get up, nor … anymore. They remained so, statues.

sentences.source_line: Maṭi u+xabro lu+qašo, u+qašo ġắlăbe roḥamwa a+bnoṯe.
sentences.translation: The news reached the priest, the priest loved his daughters very much.

items.value: Maṭi u+xabro lu+qašo, u+qašo ġắlăbe roḥamwa a+bnoṯe.
The news reached the priest, the priest loved his daughters very much.

sentences.source_line: Aṯi, mžīd qəm raġle d Mar Barṣawmo.
sentences.translation: He came, stretched out before the feet of St Barsawmo.

items.value: Aṯi, mžīd qəm raġle d Mar Barṣawmo.
He came, stretched out before the feet of St Barsawmo.

sentences.source_line: Maḥatle u+ʕafro draġle d Mar Barṣawmo ʕal qarʕe druḥe ŭ sġəḏle l Mar Barṣawmo, omar, ‘Kobaʕno d̥šorat a+bnoṯayḏi’.
sentences.translation: He put the dirt of St Barsawmo’s feet on his head, and he bowed down to St Barsawmo, he says, ‘I want you to release my daughters’.

items.value: Maḥatle u+ʕafro draġle d Mar Barṣawmo ʕal qarʕe druḥe ŭ sġəḏle l Mar Barṣawmo, omar, ‘Kobaʕno d̥šorat a+bnoṯayḏi’.
He put the dirt of St Barsawmo’s feet on his head, and he bowed down to St Barsawmo, he says, ‘I want you to release my daughters’.

sentences.source_line: Omar, ‘Məšrewu!’
sentences.translation: He says, ‘Be released!’

sentences.source_line: Naqqa šarən.
sentences.translation: At once they got released.

sentences.source_line: Ŭ azzə́n, edi twərre aṣ+ṣalmaṯṯe ŭ mət̬haymanne, mət̬haymanne bә Mšiḥo ŭ hawən səryoye.
sentences.translation: And they went, then they broke their idols and believed, they believed in Christ and became Christians.

items.value: Ŭ azzə́n, edi twərre aṣ+ṣalmaṯṯe ŭ mət̬haymanne, mət̬haymanne bә Mšiḥo ŭ hawən səryoye.
And they went, then they broke their idols and believed, they believed in Christ and became Christians.

sentences.source_line: Ŭ hun žә mə ra sāġ.
sentences.translation: And you be well for me!

items.value: Ŭ hun žә mə ra sāġ.
And you be well for me!
